history.what: stops at any sound in the caller channel
echo removal + caller enrolment + weighted evidence (offline score)
graded 'softer than the caller' rule, leaky speech, agent-text context
+ offline Whisper tiny: transcript + keyword spotting of stop / listener words
+ end of turn: pause, hesitation, words (wait / digits)

history_note: v2, v4 and v5: official real-time runs (python -m ttbench.play --calls all), decisions timed when they arrive, speech recogniser delay included. Baseline and TurnSense v3.1: offline with the same scorer (no processing delay), so v3.1 is, if anything, flattered. v5 changes nothing on the STOP path: its gain is the end-of-turn track.
asr: Whisper tiny, transcript + keyword spotting, 10 s window

failures.what: The TV talks during the agent's very first sentence. The caller has not spoken yet, so there is no caller level to compare against, and the TV is loud enough to look like the caller.
failures.fix: learn the background talker before the first stop is allowed (it is present before the agent starts), or ask the words whether the speech is addressed to the agent.

failures.what: It starts with a listener word and pauses, exactly like a backchannel. The intent only appears at «بس», so we stop 890 ms after it became evident (credit 0.70).
failures.fix: a word-order rule: «listener word + بس / لكن» is a turn claim. It needs words within ~300 ms, so a faster recogniser.

failures.what: One 450 ms word in car noise, right at an agent phrase end, then silence. Acoustically it is a backchannel, and v2 missed it.
failures.fix: done in v4: when the caller falls silent we transcribe the complete short word once, and keyword spotting confirms «لحظة».

failures.what: Isolated one-word commands. Free transcription writes «توقف» as «تبقص». Keyword spotting catches 12 of 18 isolated stop words (transcript alone: 8), with 0 of 32 listener words mistaken for a stop.
failures.fix: a larger recogniser that is still fast enough (≤ 300 ms), or a small keyword model trained on Saudi commands.

failures.said: يُمّه! وين الشاحن؟ · «بس» from the TV
failures.what: The caller talks to someone in the room, or a background voice says a stop word. Both are 7–10 dB softer than the caller's own turn, so neither the length rule nor the stop word fires.
failures.fix: a caller who shouts at the room would still cause a stop: knowing who the words are addressed to needs language understanding.

failures.what: Keyword spotting raised responsiveness on the frozen holdout (0.919 → 0.944) but turned one background-speech event into a false stop: Core 87.1 → 85.3. We kept it, because dev and xdev improved and we did not tune on the holdout.
failures.fix: require the stop word's audio to come from the caller's level range, frame by frame, not only on average.

failures.what: During dictation we took the turn once in a gap that was not labelled as a pause. The digit counting (the agent asked for seven digits) then held us until all seven were read, and we answered 560 ms after the last one.
failures.fix: count digit groups acoustically as well, so the end-of-turn layer does not depend on the recogniser hearing every digit.
